title.narrative: Georgia - TB/HIV - National Center For Disease Control and Public Health

description.narrative: Georgia - TB/HIV - National Center For Disease Control and Public Health - NCDC. This program has the following goals: To turn the HIV epidemic in the reversal phase through strengthened interventions targeting key affected populations (KAP), and significant improvement in health outcomes for PLHIV.. To decrease the burden of tuberculosis and its impact over the overall social and economic development in Georgia, by ensuring universal access to timely and quality diagnosis and treatment of all forms of TB, thus decrease illness, death and drug resistance. The objectives of this program are: Improve HIV health outcomes through ensuring universal access to quality treatment, care and support.. Ensure sustainable strong response to the epidemic through enhanced government committment, enabling legislative and operational environment, and greater involvement of civil society. Improve the effectiveness of outreach and prevention and ensure timely detection of HIV and progression to care. To provide universal access to early and quality diagnosis of all forms of TB including Drug Resistant TB. To improve treatment outcomes through universal access to quality treatment of all forms of TB including Drug Resistant TB with appropriate patient support. Scale up effective TB prevention. To strengthen the health system's cross-cutting functions and performance fot TB and HIV/AIDS control
